## Setup

The sensors form the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$. The panel is a unit square with center $C$ and rotation $\theta$. By periodicity of the lattice, fix $C$ uniformly in the fundamental cell $[-1/2,1/2]^2$, and $\theta$ uniform on $[0,2\pi)$.

The panel covers lattice point $P$ iff $C \in P + S_\theta$ (translates of the rotated square $S_\theta$ centered at origin). So for fixed $\theta$:

$$P(\text{cover}\mid\theta) = \text{area}\Big((\bigcup_{P\in\mathbb{Z}^2}(P+S_\theta))\cap[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]^2\Big).$$

By periodicity this is the area of $S_\theta$ reduced mod $1$ onto the torus $[-1/2,1/2)^2$. Since $|S_\theta|=1=$ torus area, the **uncovered** (hole) area equals the overlap area, and $P(\text{no cover}\mid\theta) = \text{hole area}$.

## Symmetry reduction

The square has dihedral symmetry $D_4$ (order 8): $f(\theta):=P(\text{no cover}\mid\theta)$ satisfies $f(\theta+\pi/2)=f(\theta)$ and $f(-\theta)=f(\theta)$. So it suffices to integrate over $[0,\pi/4]$ with factor $8/(2\pi)=4/\pi$.

## Computing the hole (fixed $\theta\in(0,\pi/4]$)

The rotated square has vertices (rotating $(\pm 1/2,\pm 1/2)$ by $\theta$):
$$V_1=(a,b),\ V_2=(-b,a),\ V_3=(-a,-b),\ V_4=(b,-a),$$
where $a=\frac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{2},\ b=\frac{\cos\theta+\sin\theta}{2}$. Note $a^2+b^2=1/2$, $b-a=\sin\theta$, $a+b=\cos\theta$, and $b\in(1/2,\sqrt2/2]$.

The square pokes out beyond $x=\pm 1/2$ and $y=\pm 1/2$ (since $b>1/2$), wrapping on the torus. Checking coverage along the edges (e.g. at $y=0$ the square spans $x\in[-1/(2\cos\theta),1/(2\cos\theta)]\supset[-1/2,1/2]$): **no holes along edges**. Holes appear only at the 4 corners of the fundamental cell.

**Corner $(1/2,1/2)$:** The relevant square edge is $V_1\to V_4$ (from $(a,b)$ to $(b,-a)$). The corner $(1/2,1/2)$ lies outside the square (cross-product test gives $(\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1)/2>0$). The wrapped parts of the square land near $x\approx-1/2$ or $y\approx-1/2$, not near $(1/2,1/2)$. So the hole is the triangle cut off by $x=1/2$, $y=1/2$, and edge $V_1V_4$.

Edge $V_1V_4$ meets $x=1/2$ at $P_x=(1/2,\ \tfrac{1-a-b}{2(b-a)})$ and meets $y=1/2$ at $P_y=(\tfrac{1+a-b}{2(a+b)},\ 1/2)$. The triangle (vertices $(1/2,1/2),P_x,P_y$) has legs
$$\tfrac{1-2b}{2(b-a)}\ \text{and}\ \tfrac{1-2b}{2(a+b)},$$
so
$$\text{Area}_{\text{one}}=\frac{(2b-1)^2}{8(b-a)(a+b)}=\frac{(\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1)^2}{8\sin\theta\cos\theta}.$$

By 4-fold symmetry, total hole area:
$$f(\theta)=\frac{(\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1)^2}{\sin 2\theta}.$$

**Checks:** $f\to 0$ as $\theta\to 0$ ✓ (axis-aligned panel always hits a corner). At $\theta=\pi/4$: $f=(\sqrt2-1)^2=3-2\sqrt2\approx0.172$ ✓ (diamond leaves 4 corner triangles of total area $3-2\sqrt2$).

## Integration

$$P=\frac{4}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{(\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1)^2}{\sin 2\theta}\,d\theta.$$

Expand the numerator: $(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2-2(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)+1 = 2+\sin 2\theta -2\cos\theta-2\sin\theta$. Dividing by $\sin 2\theta$:
$$\frac{2}{\sin 2\theta}+1-\frac{1}{\sin\theta}-\frac{1}{\cos\theta}=2\csc 2\theta+1-\csc\theta-\sec\theta.$$

(At $\theta\to0$ this tends to $0$, so the integral is proper.) Using
$$\int 2\csc 2\theta\,d\theta=\ln|\tan\theta|,\quad \int\csc\theta\,d\theta=\ln|\tan(\theta/2)|,\quad \int\sec\theta\,d\theta=\ln|\sec\theta+\tan\theta|,$$

$$I=\Big[\ln\tan\theta+\theta-\ln\tan(\theta/2)-\ln(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)\Big]_0^{\pi/4}.$$

At $\theta=\pi/4$: $\tan=1$, $\tan(\pi/8)=\sqrt2-1$, $\sec+\tan=\sqrt2+1$:
$$0+\tfrac{\pi}{4}-\ln(\sqrt2-1)-\ln(\sqrt2+1)=\tfrac{\pi}{4}-\ln\big((\sqrt2-1)(\sqrt2+1)\big)=\tfrac{\pi}{4}-\ln 1=\tfrac{\pi}{4}.$$

At $\theta\to0$: $\ln\tan\theta-\ln\tan(\theta/2)\to\ln 2$, and $\ln(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)\to 0$, $\theta\to 0$; value $=\ln 2$.

Therefore $I=\pi/4-\ln 2$, and

$$\boxed{P=\frac{4}{\pi}\Big(\frac{\pi}{4}-\ln 2\Big)=1-\frac{4\ln 2}{\pi}.}$$

Numerically: $4\ln 2/\pi\approx 0.8825$, so $P\approx 0.1175$ — consistent with $f$ ranging from $0$ to $\approx0.172$ over $[0,\pi/4]$.

## Setup

The sensors form the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$. The panel is a unit square with center $C$ and rotation $\theta$. By periodicity of the lattice, fix $C$ uniformly in the fundamental cell $[-1/2,1/2]^2$, and $\theta$ uniform on $[0,2\pi)$.

The panel covers lattice point $P$ iff $C \in P + S_\theta$ (translates of the rotated square $S_\theta$ centered at origin). So for fixed $\theta$:

$$P(\text{cover}\mid\theta) = \text{area}\Big((\bigcup_{P\in\mathbb{Z}^2}(P+S_\theta))\cap[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]^2\Big).$$

By periodicity this is the area of $S_\theta$ reduced mod $1$ onto the torus $[-1/2,1/2)^2$. Since $|S_\theta|=1=$ torus area, the **uncovered** (hole) area equals the overlap area, and $P(\text{no cover}\mid\theta) = \text{hole area}$.

## Symmetry reduction

The square has dihedral symmetry $D_4$ (order 8): $f(\theta):=P(\text{no cover}\mid\theta)$ satisfies $f(\theta+\pi/2)=f(\theta)$ and $f(-\theta)=f(\theta)$. So it suffices to integrate over $[0,\pi/4]$ with factor $8/(2\pi)=4/\pi$.

## Computing the hole (fixed $\theta\in(0,\pi/4]$)

The rotated square has vertices (rotating $(\pm 1/2,\pm 1/2)$ by $\theta$):
$$V_1=(a,b),\ V_2=(-b,a),\ V_3=(-a,-b),\ V_4=(b,-a),$$
where $a=\frac{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}{2},\ b=\frac{\cos\theta+\sin\theta}{2}$. Note $a^2+b^2=1/2$, $b-a=\sin\theta$, $a+b=\cos\theta$, and $b\in(1/2,\sqrt2/2]$.

The square pokes out beyond $x=\pm 1/2$ and $y=\pm 1/2$ (since $b>1/2$), wrapping on the torus. Checking coverage along the edges (e.g. at $y=0$ the square spans $x\in[-1/(2\cos\theta),1/(2\cos\theta)]\supset[-1/2,1/2]$): **no holes along edges**. Holes appear only at the 4 corners of the fundamental cell.

**Corner $(1/2,1/2)$:** The relevant square edge is $V_1\to V_4$ (from $(a,b)$ to $(b,-a)$). The corner $(1/2,1/2)$ lies outside the square (cross-product test gives $(\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1)/2>0$). The wrapped parts of the square land near $x\approx-1/2$ or $y\approx-1/2$, not near $(1/2,1/2)$. So the hole is the triangle cut off by $x=1/2$, $y=1/2$, and edge $V_1V_4$.

Edge $V_1V_4$ meets $x=1/2$ at $P_x=(1/2,\ \tfrac{1-a-b}{2(b-a)})$ and meets $y=1/2$ at $P_y=(\tfrac{1+a-b}{2(a+b)},\ 1/2)$. The triangle (vertices $(1/2,1/2),P_x,P_y$) has legs
$$\tfrac{1-2b}{2(b-a)}\ \text{and}\ \tfrac{1-2b}{2(a+b)},$$
so
$$\text{Area}_{\text{one}}=\frac{(2b-1)^2}{8(b-a)(a+b)}=\frac{(\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1)^2}{8\sin\theta\cos\theta}.$$

By 4-fold symmetry, total hole area:
$$f(\theta)=\frac{(\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1)^2}{\sin 2\theta}.$$

**Checks:** $f\to 0$ as $\theta\to 0$ ✓ (axis-aligned panel always hits a corner). At $\theta=\pi/4$: $f=(\sqrt2-1)^2=3-2\sqrt2\approx0.172$ ✓ (diamond leaves 4 corner triangles of total area $3-2\sqrt2$).

## Integration

$$P=\frac{4}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi/4}\frac{(\cos\theta+\sin\theta-1)^2}{\sin 2\theta}\,d\theta.$$

Expand the numerator: $(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)^2-2(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)+1 = 2+\sin 2\theta -2\cos\theta-2\sin\theta$. Dividing by $\sin 2\theta$:
$$\frac{2}{\sin 2\theta}+1-\frac{1}{\sin\theta}-\frac{1}{\cos\theta}=2\csc 2\theta+1-\csc\theta-\sec\theta.$$

(At $\theta\to0$ this tends to $0$, so the integral is proper.) Using
$$\int 2\csc 2\theta\,d\theta=\ln|\tan\theta|,\quad \int\csc\theta\,d\theta=\ln|\tan(\theta/2)|,\quad \int\sec\theta\,d\theta=\ln|\sec\theta+\tan\theta|,$$

$$I=\Big[\ln\tan\theta+\theta-\ln\tan(\theta/2)-\ln(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)\Big]_0^{\pi/4}.$$

At $\theta=\pi/4$: $\tan=1$, $\tan(\pi/8)=\sqrt2-1$, $\sec+\tan=\sqrt2+1$:
$$0+\tfrac{\pi}{4}-\ln(\sqrt2-1)-\ln(\sqrt2+1)=\tfrac{\pi}{4}-\ln\big((\sqrt2-1)(\sqrt2+1)\big)=\tfrac{\pi}{4}-\ln 1=\tfrac{\pi}{4}.$$

At $\theta\to0$: $\ln\tan\theta-\ln\tan(\theta/2)\to\ln 2$, and $\ln(\sec\theta+\tan\theta)\to 0$, $\theta\to 0$; value $=\ln 2$.

Therefore $I=\pi/4-\ln 2$, and

$$\boxed{P=\frac{4}{\pi}\Big(\frac{\pi}{4}-\ln 2\Big)=1-\frac{4\ln 2}{\pi}.}$$

Numerically: $4\ln 2/\pi\approx 0.8825$, so $P\approx 0.1175$ — consistent with $f$ ranging from $0$ to $\approx0.172$ over $[0,\pi/4]$.
